title: Massaman Chicken Curry with Potatoes and Toasted Whole Spices
summary: Whole spices are toasted, ground and mixed with red curry paste, fried in coconut cream, then simmered with coconut milk, potatoes, browned chicken thighs, peanuts, fish sauce, palm sugar and tamarind until thick.
equipment: spice grinder or mortar and pestle
large heavy pot or casserole (about 5 l)

ingredients.note: check the label: most Thai curry pastes contain shrimp paste (crustaceans); choose a shrimp-free paste if you avoid it

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 4 cm pieces
waxy potatoes, cut into 3 cm cubes
roasted unsalted peanuts, plus 15 g chopped to serve
palm sugar or light brown sugar

steps.title: Toast the spices
steps.text: Toast 3 cardamom pods, 1 tsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, the cinnamon stick and 4 cloves in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 2 min. Grind finely and mix with the pinch of nutmeg and 60 g red curry paste.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat and brown 800 g chicken pieces in batches, about 3 min per side. Set aside.

steps.title: Fry the paste
steps.text: Spoon the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into the pot and fry the spice paste in it, stirring, until fragrant and the oil separates, 3 to 5 min. Add the shallots and cook until soft, about 3 min.

steps.title: Reduce
steps.text: Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and boil gently for 10 min until slightly thickened.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add 450 g potatoes and simmer 10 min, then add the chicken, 50 g peanuts, 4 tsp fish sauce, 10 g palm sugar and 2 tsp tamarind. Simmer, partly covered, until the potatoes are tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C, 20 to 25 min.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Taste and balance the sweet, sour and salty notes, then rest 5 min so the oil rises. Serve with rice, scattered with coriander and the chopped peanuts.

tips: Toast the spices only until fragrant; burnt spices turn bitter.
Thighs stay juicier than breast in a long simmer.
Taste for the sweet, sour and salty balance before serving.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat once until piping hot. It freezes well for up to 3 months, though the potatoes soften. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
